assumptions: Latency is measured in milliseconds on the cleaned attempts view.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct (341 attempts ingested twice) were removed before computing this figure, so each attempt is counted once.
Attempt volume was 39% above the usual level from 18 Oct to 31 Oct. This is not a data error by itself, but it may mean the late-October period is not typical.

facts.text: The p95 authorization latency for CREDIT_CARD payments from 1 Oct to 31 Oct 2026 was 6,344.6 ms.
On 12 Oct, 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts); duplicates were removed from the clean view that this metric uses.
Attempt volume ran 39% above the usual level for those weekdays between 18 Oct and 31 Oct.

response.headline: The p95 authorization latency for credit card payments in October 2026 was about 6,345 ms (roughly 6.3 seconds), meaning 95% of attempts completed at or below that time.

recommendations.rationale: A single p95 value has no baseline; a comparison would show whether October is normal or elevated.
recommendations.text: If you want to judge whether 6.3 seconds is high, compare it with September or with other payment methods using the same p95 metric.

recommendations.rationale: Higher volume can coincide with different latency behaviour, so the period may not be typical.
